method: Ratios pair control/candidate by trial index. Bootstrap resamples those 15 pairs, 10000 replicates, fixed seed. Intervals are descriptive: serial batches and shared heaps violate independent-trial assumptions. Ratio of medians and median paired ratio are distinct estimators. No multiple-comparison correction, no subtraction of A/A or source shifts.
limitations: Single VM/browser and canvas profile; four workloads only.
A/A uses 500ms warmup; candidate first-use uses1000ms. Counts differ on some rows, notably ER first-render. It diagnoses instance/run variation, not a rowwise correction.

Source and post-first-render lanes do not execute initial packed publication in timed work. Their shifts demonstrate unresolved control variation or indirect effects; neither random noise nor a packed CPU mechanism is proven.
54 browser E2E passed according to parent; this analysis does not rerun them. Correctness does not establish performance.

conclusion.coldParse: All four ratio-of-medians results are slower: +0.31% to +7.69%; no demonstrated parse gain.
conclusion.firstUse: Eight of ten actual first-use ratio-of-medians results are slower; ER unchanged first-render and Gantt callback are modestly lower. Gantt first invoke +5.01%. No complete-lifecycle win justifies adoption.
conclusion.controls: Flowchart source shifts upward in both candidate reports (+2.81%, +4.23%); several other source rows also rise. Identical-runtime A/A ranges -5.73% to +1.30%. These limit precise attribution; they do not rescue the unsuccessful candidate.
hypothesesOnly: Initial string conversion uses Uint16Array.subarray followed by spread; legacy uses an ordinary Array slice followed by spread. Both allocate a view/slice; V8 can optimize their iteration differently. Source cannot establish a typed-array penalty.

Direct publication re-reads tags, lengths, keys and atom payloads via DataView after validation; legacy loads decoded JS fields. Allocation savings trade against repeated byte reads, switches and bounds checks. Source cannot establish their sampled weight.

First invoke/edited render/callback materializes the entire legacy graph after already publishing packed state, creating deferred decode work. This is definite extra work in that path, but its share of observed latency is unmeasured.
Although this candidate removed the predecessor full-frame copy and second reference pass, it retained those string/publication tradeoffs. Lower retained object count alone is insufficient evidence.
